title: Separability descends from a tensor field after scalar extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ and $k\subseteq F$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose that the commutative tensor algebra $F\otimes_k k'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$, is a field and is separable over $k'$ in the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every intermediate field finitely generated over $k'$ is separably generated. Then $F/k$ is separable in that same sense. Neither extension is assumed algebraic or finitely generated.

source.place: Tags 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, and 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions; faithful extension of scalars and a common extension field give the stated descent corollary. Applies to the corrected tensor-field identification in more-algebra.tex Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type.

proof.text: Put $T=F\otimes_k k'$, with its given field structure. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] applied to $F/k$ proves the conclusion. Henceforth let $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$; since $k$ is a field, $p$ is prime.

source.place: Tag 00TX, lemma-characteristic-zero-local-smooth, first sentence of proof; characteristic-zero branch separated from Tag 030W

proof.text: Fix any field extension $L/k$. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to $L/k$ and $k'/k$, obtaining a field $M$ and compatible $k$-embeddings $i:L\to M$ and $j:k'\to M$. Regard $M$ as a $k'$-algebra through $j$. No embedding of either $L$ or $k'$ into the other is being assumed.

We show that $T\otimes_{k'}M$ is reduced. A nilpotent $x$ is a finite sum $\sum_r t_r\otimes m_r$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $E=k'(t_1,\ldots,t_s)\subseteq T$. The separability hypothesis on $T/k'$, using [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (2), says precisely that $E/k'$ is separably generated. The field $M$ is reduced, so [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] gives reducedness of $E\otimes_{k'}M$. Its map into $T\otimes_{k'}M$ is injective: $M$ is flat over $k'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], and [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applies to the inclusion $E\hookrightarrow T$ (interchanging tensor factors by $e\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes e$). The element $y=\sum_r t_r\otimes m_r$ in this smaller tensor ring maps to $x$. If $x^n=0$ for $n>0$, injectivity gives $y^n=0$, hence $y=0$ by reducedness and $x=0$. This proves the claim without assuming that $T/k'$ is finitely generated or separably generated.

source.place: Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, separable case: reduction to finitely generated subextensions; explicit finite-tensor argument

proof.text: There is a ring isomorphism $\Phi:T\otimes_{k'}M\to F\otimes_k M$ given by $\Phi((a\otimes b)\otimes m)=a\otimes j(b)m$, with inverse $\Psi(a\otimes m)=(a\otimes1)\otimes m$. The tensor universal properties [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give these maps: the displayed formulas are additive and balanced over $k$ and $k'$, and preserve products and units on pure tensors. Their composites fix $a\otimes m$ and $(a\otimes b)\otimes m$, respectively, the latter because $(a\otimes b)\otimes m=(a\otimes1)\otimes j(b)m$. Pure tensors generate, so the composites are identities. If $z$ in $F\otimes_k M$ is nilpotent, $\Psi(z)$ is nilpotent and hence zero by step 3; applying $\Phi$ shows $z=0$.

source.place: Tags 030U and 030W descent corollary: explicit tensor reassociation from the tensor universal property

proof.text: The map $1_F\otimes i:F\otimes_k L\to F\otimes_k M$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] applied to the $k$-vector space $F$ and [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applied to the injective $k$-linear map $i:L\to M$. It is a ring homomorphism by the tensor product multiplication. Every nilpotent $z$ in its source maps to a nilpotent in its reduced target, hence to zero; injectivity gives $z=0$. Thus $F\otimes_k L$ is reduced. Since $L/k$ was arbitrary, this holds for every field extension of $k$.

source.place: Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, condition (4); reducedness descends through the explicitly injective scalar-extension map

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-reduced-extension-separable] to $F/k$ and the prime $p$. Its characteristic hypothesis is step 1, and its reducedness hypothesis for every $L/k$ is step 5. It gives exactly that every finitely generated intermediate field of $F/k$ is separably generated, which is the required separability. No algebraicity or finite-generation hypothesis on $F/k$ or $k'/k$ has entered.

proof_origin.place: Descent corollary assembled from Tags 030U and 030W using the common field of Fields Tag 0H7K; finite-coefficient and tensor-reassociation arguments written explicitly.
